add.issue.name: The log pane and the ticket panel keep their headers on one line

edit.description.md:
The two panes flanking the board set their headers differently: the event log's header row sits flush against the top edge (`padding: 0 …`), while the ticket/diff panel keeps the aside's own 20px inset. Read across the board the two rows of buttons are ~13px apart.

Give the log header the aside's inset and the height of an icon button, so both header bands occupy the same line.

add.issue.name: A ticket ref in prose lights under the pointer

edit.description.md:
A ref linkified in a description or a comment opens a preview card on hover, but the word itself does not react: same colour, same underline, resting and hovered. Until the card's delay elapses nothing says it is pressable.

Give it a hover state in the app's own idiom — a wash of its own colour, as a tag chip takes — without moving the line it sits in.

Regression test in `panel-header.pw.ts`, red at 18px apart without the change.

Put all three on one inset, named once rather than restated at each, and make that inset shallower: 20px is more empty space than the top of the window needs.

add.issue.name: The fullscreen lanes test is found by a title the tooltip layer takes away

edit.description.md:
`fullscreen-lanes.pw.ts` locates the panel's fullscreen toggle with `getByTitle('Exit fullscreen')`. `TooltipLayer` removes a `title` when it opens its own tooltip over the element, parking the text in `data-epiq-tip` — and the test's own click leaves the pointer sitting on that button, so the tooltip opens and the attribute goes.

Whether the test passes is then a race between the tooltip's hover delay and how fast Playwright reaches the locator. Alone it wins; under the pre-push gate, which runs the browser suite beside the docker suites, it loses — it failed four gate runs in a row while passing standalone and at `--repeat-each=6`. The failure's page snapshot shows the panel correctly in fullscreen with the button present, unnamed, and a `tooltip "Exit fullscreen"` beside it.

Give the toggle a test id and locate it by that. This is the flake that has been blocking pushes.

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `03fff446`. `FullscreenToggleButton` now carries `testId="fullscreen-toggle"` and the spec locates it by that in all five places; the `title` stays for the tooltip itself.

The mechanism, confirmed with a throwaway probe rather than inferred: click the toggle, leave the pointer on it, wait past the tooltip delay — `getByTitle('Exit fullscreen')` then matches **zero** elements while `getByTestId('fullscreen-toggle')` still resolves. The four gate failures' page snapshot agrees: panel correctly in fullscreen, lanes drawn, button present but unnamed, and a `tooltip "Exit fullscreen"` beside it.

So it was never a timing problem in the app, and never load as such — load only changed which side of the race won. Every other `getByTitle` in the suite is exposed to the same thing wherever a click leaves the pointer on the element; those have not bitten yet and are not touched here.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.name: Card and column spacing: one rhythm instead of three

edit.description.md:
A ticket card's internal rhythm is `gap: 12` between title, ref and tags, but its own box padding is 16 and the gap between cards is 8 — so internal air is twice the separation, and with a 6%-opacity fill doing the boundary work a column of cards runs together.

- card padding 16 → 12, so the edge inset matches the rhythm it contains
- gap between cards 8 → 12
- `COLUMN_PADDING` 14 → 12

Measured: cards 119px → 111px, gaps 8 → 12, 127 → 123 per card, so slightly more fits in a column.

The scrollbar gutter derives from the column padding (`COLUMN_PADDING / 2`) and moves with it — it is not hardcoded.

add.issue.name: The right panel's header is a band above the pane, not a row inside it

edit.description.md:
The panel on the right scrolled its own header away, and its scrollbar ran the full height of the panel — up beside the header and 20px in from the panel's edge. The log on the other side of the board does neither, because its header sits outside its scrolling pane.

Give the right panel the same structure:

- `Aside` renders a header band above the pane; `FormHeader` lands in it through a context slot, so a panel still writes its header where it reads it (the ticket's ref, the lane's title and the fullscreen state are all mid-render values that a `header` prop would mean computing twice).
- All four right-panel modes share that band — `SwimlaneStats` and `BulkDetails` hand-rolled their own header row and now use `FormHeader` too.
- The pane's scrollbar sits in the gutter, half the panel padding in, by the same rule the board's columns use (`lib/scroll-gutter.style.ts`, shared).
- Header padding `8px` top and bottom, with the rule under it that the log's header draws; `PANE_HEADER_INSET` 10 → 8 and `LOG_PANE_PADDING_X` 14 → 12 so both headers read `8px 12px 8px 30px` / `8px 0`.

add.issue.name: The narrow-to-ticket control wears a funnel, not the timeline's own mark

edit.description.md:
`TicketOnlyToggle` and the scrubber's collapse toggle both drew `IconTimeline`, so one mark meant "the timeline" in one place and "a filter over the timeline" in the other, on the same screen.

The scrubber's keeps it — it is the timeline. The panel's control is a filter, so it takes a funnel, as devtools and spreadsheets draw one.

add.issue.name: The board's page margin is 4px, named once, and a card's wash is a step clear of the background

edit.description.md:
Two things the board was spending on nothing:

- `<main>` carried a literal `0 0 0 30px`, and `BOARD_GUTTER = 30` restated it for the spacer that ends the column row — a comment tied them together and nothing else did. Now one constant at 4, read by both, so the board's two page margins cannot drift apart.
- A resting card's `rgba(185, 192, 255, 0.06)` is hard to pick out of the page. Raised to `0.08`; the selected card's wash goes `0.08` → `0.11` with it, or a picked card would be the same weight as a resting one and only its hue would say so.

add.issue.name: The chrome sits on its own black ground, below the board

edit.description.md:
The top bar, the timeline and the event log were drawn on the page's own ground or on `panel`, which put the instrumentation on the same plane as the work, or in front of it.

They now take `GUI_THEME.chrome` (`#000000`), below the board's `bg`. Three grounds, deepest first: chrome `#000` → board `#06070a` → panel `#11141b`. The log takes it on the vertical axis and the bar on the horizontal, so the chrome reads as one L around the work. `LogWindow` — the popped-out log — takes it too, or the same log would differ by where it is shown.

No dimming. An opacity pass over the log's text was tried and dropped: measured against the current design it costs contrast on every tone (`dim` 2.85 → 2.41 at 0.8), while the black ground on its own *raises* every one of them (`dim` 2.85 → 3.25, `primary` 10.70 → 12.19). The recession comes free from the ground.

add.issue.name: Direction: a command line along the bottom of the GUI, speaking the TUI's language

edit.description.md:
Raised by the user on 2026-09-19 while the chrome moved onto its own black ground (`ADZD1MC`): the terminal feel suggests a terminal, so a command line at the foot of the window that takes the same commands the TUI does.

**Not started, and not to be started without the user's word.** Recorded so the direction is on the board rather than in a chat log.

What is already there, from a read of the code rather than a guess:

- The GUI's palette and the TUI already share a vocabulary. `GuiCommandId = CmdKeyword | 'gui:${string}'` in `gui/client/lib/commands/command.model.ts`, and a test holds the first half to `CmdKeywords` so the two cannot drift apart silently.
- What differs is the surface, not the meaning: the GUI palette is a **picker** (fuzzy match, two-stage arguments), the TUI is a **parser** — `command-parser.ts`, `command-modifiers.ts`, `command-auto-complete.ts`, `command-validation.ts`. A bottom command line is the parser's surface, driving the registry the palette already drives.

The open question to settle first: whether the TUI's parser can be imported by the client at all. `source/lib/command-line/**` is on the wrong side of the browser/Node boundary — see the note that importing from it pulls Node-only files into the client's type program and fails `npm run build:gui` — yet `cmd-keywords.js` is imported from there today and is fine. So the answer is per-module and has to be measured, not assumed. Until then, the cost of this is unknown: it is either a small reuse or a port of the parser into the client.

Second question for the user: what a command line is **for** when the palette already exists. Typing speed for people who know the words, a place for commands with arguments the palette handles awkwardly, or the terminal feel itself.

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: `6226e9bc` (PR #357). `GUI_THEME.chrome` read by a wrapper around the bar and the timeline, by the log's panel and by `LogWindow`. No dimming — the measurement is in the description.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `10bbb87e` and `dd0d0a57` (PR #357). `Aside` renders the band and provides `AsideHeaderSlot`; `FormHeader` portals into it, so all four right-panel modes share one header that stays put while the pane scrolls beneath it, with the scrollbar confined to the body and sitting in the gutter (`lib/scroll-gutter.style.ts`, shared with the board's columns).

Two tests needed real repair rather than a locator swap:

- `aside-stacking.pw.ts` engineered a **one-pixel** overlap between the scrubber's filter popover and the panel's diff header, and its own comment warned that any change to the chrome's height would erase it. This one did, by 4px. It now opens the contributors row of the filter — the only one of the four with entries on a fresh board — which pushes the list 19px past the pane, so the overlap is made rather than inherited. That row's disclosure gained `data-testid="filter-axis-<axis>"` on the way, since it had none and a `title` is not a handle.
- `ref-preview.pw.ts` looked for the ref button before waiting for the description that holds it, so a panel still showing the previous ticket read as a ref that failed to linkify. It waits for the text first.

add.issue.name: The board switcher moves up into the topbar, and the lanes rise with it

edit.description.md:
The switcher sits in a row of its own above the columns (`App.tsx`, the row at `PANE_HEADER_INSET`), which costs ~56px at the top of the board and puts it *below* the timeline it governs — `TimeScrubber` takes `boardId` and re-fetches history on it.

Move it into the topbar as a breadcrumb: `:epiq / Default ⌄`, then the ⌘K hint. That ground never collapses and spans everything below it.

Not into the scrubber's control row, where it was first suggested: that group is swapped out wholesale when the timeline is collapsed (`ScrubberLayout.tsx`), and the collapse is remembered across loads, so the switcher would vanish for good. The fixtures well that survives is two icon buttons wide and means "which panels are open".

Consequence to settle by eye: `lib/pane-header.style.ts` says three rows across the window read as one line — the log's fields, this switcher, the ticket panel's ref row. With the switcher gone the lane headers rise into that line instead. Expected to read better (three real pane headers), but wants a pixel check and a pass over the e2e chrome-height assumptions.

Keep `testId="board-switcher"` so the existing specs follow it.

add.issue.name: A lane lights from further off: the column glow's reach goes 200 → 250

edit.description.md:
`SwimlaneColumn` passes `proximityReach={200}` to `Panel` — how far outside the column the pointer still lights its border. Asked for 50 more, so a column answers from further away.

Only the reach moves. `glowRadius` (370) is the size of the wash itself and stays as it is.

add.issue.name: The log's field boxes fold into a menu when the pane is too narrow for the row

edit.description.md:
Narrow the log pane and its header runs off the edge: `Label`, the split button and the pop-out are clipped by the panel rather than reflowing. The row neither wraps nor shrinks, and shouldn't — it is read against the pane headers beside it, and a second line would push the first log line down out of that reading.

Fold instead: under `LOG_HEADER_FOLD_WIDTH` the five boxes collapse behind one `Fields ⌄` control that drops them as the same checkboxes, in the same order. The split and pop-out buttons keep their place at the far end.

A width, not a measurement of the row: once folded, what the row measures is the folded row, so measuring would fold and unfold forever at the width where it just fits. Threshold tuned by eye.

add.issue.name: The log's board-facing edge is drawn like the ticket panel's

edit.description.md:
The log pane's right edge was a `line` hairline — the colour that divides sections *inside* a panel. The ticket panel on the other side of the board wears `edge` plus a shadow cast at the board, so it reads as a surface in front of the board rather than as more of it. The log takes the same treatment, mirrored.

Its ground stays `chrome`, unlike the panel's `panel`: the log is instrumentation, and the two are deliberately on different grounds.

add.issue.name: The board switcher's list says how many issues each board holds

edit.description.md:
As the TUI's board list does (`BoardList.tsx`: `Title (N issues)`). In the GUI it goes dim and right-aligned in the open list, before the tick — not on the trigger, which is sized to the name and would clip it.

Counted client-side: the state carries every board's lanes and their issues, not only the board on screen, so nothing new is asked of the server.

`plural` moves from `issue-stats.style` to `gui-format.helper` on the way — the switcher counting issues is not a ticket's statistics.

add.issue.name: The chrome's panels open and close with a short transition instead of jumping

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `90cda10a`, plus `60fbbd00` for its colour. PR #391.

The switcher is a breadcrumb in the topbar — `:epiq / Default ⌄`, then the ⌘K hint — and `<main>` keeps no inset of its own, so the columns start on the panes' top edge and each lane's 48px header carries the gap above its title. `pane-header.style.ts` now describes two rows across the window rather than three.

Two things the move turned up:

- the topbar is a `Panel`, which clips its children to contain its glow, so the list is portalled to the body and anchored to the trigger — `useDismissOnOutsideClick` already took a portalled panel's ref for exactly this;
- a portalled list inherits the body's font, not the tree the app sets its face on, so the options came out serif. `UI_FONT` is now one export in `gui-theme`, replacing four copies of the same stack (App, LogWindow, InitProjectScreen) and stated on the popover.

`theatre.pw.ts` clicked the switcher as somewhere harmless to click; it answers with a list now, so that moved to the wordmark. `panel-header.pw.ts` was rewritten for two rows and the board's top edge.

The colour: it sat at `primary`, a neutral grey among blue-greys. Now `chromePrimary`, `primary`'s brightness with `primarySoft`'s tint.

Dropdown.tsx and App.tsx carry `632A02T`'s list markup in these commits too — prettier had re-indented both tickets' lines into one hunk.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md: Solution: `5c31c48f`. `proximityReach` 200 → 250 in `SwimlaneColumn`; `glowRadius` left at 370, since that sizes the wash rather than the distance it answers from.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `599009de`. `LogFieldsMenu` holds the trigger and the popover; `LogFieldBox` is the one box both it and the open row draw, so the fold cannot drift from the row it stands in for — same tick, same title, same standing down for the field a lane heading speaks.

The threshold was measured rather than guessed: the five boxes end 319px in and the buttons at the far end begin 60px from the right, so they meet at 379. `LOG_HEADER_FOLD_WIDTH` is 400, which keeps the gap the rest of the row keeps.

Test in `event-log.pw.ts`, checked red with the fold disabled: it asserts the menu replaces the boxes and that every control the header carries lies inside the pane — the symptom itself, not a proxy for it.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `5faf14d8`. The log's `<aside>` takes `edge` and `10px 0 24px rgba(0,0,0,0.45)` — the ticket panel's treatment, mirrored, since the board is on the other side of it. Ground stays `chrome`.

That commit's hunk also carries `9H4ENW8`'s width transition on the same element: both are the aside's style block, and prettier had them in one hunk.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `8077fd9f`, tick column in `d5b946cc`. `DropdownItem` takes a `hint`, drawn dim and right-aligned; App counts each board's lanes, which the state carries for every board and not only the one on screen. `plural` moved from `issue-stats.style` to `gui-format.helper`.

The tick used to take its width only on the selected row, which pushed that row's count out of line with the ones below; it now keeps a `1ch` column on every row and is empty on all but one.

The list's markup rides in `A4M82FD`'s commits — prettier had re-indented both tickets' lines into the same hunk of `Dropdown.tsx`.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7

add.issue.comment.md:
Solution: `7e15fe20`. `useReveal` holds a panel mounted for the length of its closing move and reports `shown` (the size to draw at) and `settled` (the move is over, so whatever clips it can let go).

Two frames, not one, before opening: a single `requestAnimationFrame` still runs before the browser has painted the mount, so both sizes land in one frame and nothing animates. Measured mid-flight rather than eyeballed — the log went 0 → 441 in one step until the second frame was added, and now reads 247 at 80ms.

- log: `width` on the aside, with the content held at the open width inside so nothing reflows on the way out — the header's own fold would otherwise trip on every close;
- timeline: a grid row between `0fr` and `1fr`, so nothing has to know how tall the charts are. The clip is let go at `settled`, because the needle's grip, the pager's arrows and the scope outline all draw past the track's edges;
- a series switched off: the commit track stays mounted in volume layout and folds to nothing, and the gap either side closes with it rather than snapping.

All of it stops at `usePrefersReducedMotion`.

The pane now says `data-settled` out loud: two tests grabbed its edge straight after opening it and were measuring a place the edge had already left.
add.issue.comment.author: PMTJJK5EF98A3YQ56J1JNFFJD7
